asian-drama.label: Asian Drama
asian-drama.description: Marks any show from an Asian country — Thailand, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, China, the Philippines, and so on — regardless of which category it lives in (LGBTQ+ Visual Media, K-dramas, or Asian Dramas). Use this tag to browse across all of them at once.

bl.label: BL (Boys' Love)
bl.description:
A genre of Asian dramas (Thailand, Taiwan, Japan, Korea, the Philippines...) centered on romance between men. Fair warning before you start: the cultural codes are different! Expect blatant product placement, cheesy soundtracks, cartoonish sound effects, and occasionally questionable acting — the genre is often more caricature than realistic representation, with lots of fanservice.

A bit of context helps it all make sense. Studios work with assigned actor pairs, so you'll often see the same two actors starring in dramas together. I find this both good and bad: on one hand, it lets them build a lot of trust and complicity with their scene partner, and you can tell their chemistry and acting usually improve in their next project. On the other, the system exists to encourage the shipping of real people — which sometimes results in unhealthy parasocial relationships and expectations — and it also limits the actors to the BL genre. And one more thing: Thai people have officially registered "nicknames", which is why actors and characters often go by names like Bible, Earth, Gun, Pond, and other random words. It's not their name, it's their nickname — totally normal in Thailand.

All that said: there are real pearls in there, and the good ones subvert all of it. Survive the first episodes and trust the process.

gl.label: GL (Girls' Love)
gl.description: The sapphic counterpart of BL. Still criminally rare — treasure every one you find.

skam-universe.label: SKAM & its remakes
skam-universe.description: SKAM is a Norwegian teen drama where each season follows one student from the same Oslo friend group — sensitive, realistic, kind of a better Skins. It became such a phenomenon that a bunch of countries remade it (France, Germany, Italy, Belgium...), each telling roughly the same stories in its own way. Comparing the versions is half the fun. In basically every version, season 3 is the gay one. You can start any season without watching the others.

free-on-youtube.label: Free on YouTube
free-on-youtube.description: Full episodes officially and freely available on YouTube, usually with English subtitles. Thai studios like GMMTV upload everything — bless them.

bl-royalty.label: BL royalty
bl-royalty.description: The crown jewels of the genre — the essentials. If you only ever watch a few BLs, make it these.

gmmtv.label: GMMTV
gmmtv.description: The giant Thai studio behind most modern Thai BLs. They manage the actor pairs, produce a dozen shows a year, and upload full episodes to YouTube for free with subtitles.

director-paof.label: Director: P'Aof
director-paof.description: P'Aof Noppharnach — my favorite director. He makes the tearjerkers, the grounded ones, the ones with the best acting (Bad Buddy, A Tale of a Thousand Stars, Moonlight Chicken, Last Twilight). He's very good friends with P'Jojo — they have an extended friend group who are all gay and have reacted to some of their shows together.

director-pjojo.label: Director: P'Jojo
director-pjojo.description: P'Jojo doesn't lean into the BL tropes and clichés — his shows are raw, messy, and honest (Only Friends, The Heart Killers). He also tends to work with the good actors. Good friends with P'Aof.

director-pgolf.label: Director: P'Golf
director-pgolf.description: P'Golf always appears in their own shows — in three different ones they show up as 'P'Golf', an LGBT café owner. Look for the cameo.

director-pnuchy.label: Director: P'Nuchy
director-pnuchy.description: Anucha 'Nuchy' Boonyawatana — a trans woman director engaged in LGBTQ+ causes. The director who least adapts to the BL format and loves pushing the envelope. She has high standards and so far has only worked with OffGun (I think).

political.label: Politically engaged
political.description: Dramas that are used to protest something or bring awareness to an issue — shows that talk about LGBTQ+ and social justice directly instead of just using it for views.

lus-favorites.label: Lu's favorites
lus-favorites.description: My personal pantheon. If it has this tag, I will defend it with my life.

casual-watching.label: Casual watching
casual-watching.description: Background shows — the ones I put on while doing other things. Low commitment, no plot stress.

lots-of-sex.label: Content note: lots of sex
lots-of-sex.description: These ones are spicy. Maybe don't watch on the bus.

disability.label: Disability representation
disability.description: Shows with meaningful disability representation in main storylines — not just as a plot device.
